summary: Explains why RFC 2190, the first RTP payload format for ITU-T H.263 video, should be moved to historic status. It is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: An old way to send a video format over the internet has been replaced. This explains why the old rulebook is retired.

questions: what is the rtp payload format for h.263
subtitle: Recommends retiring the original RTP payload format for H.263 video in favor of the newer one.

tldr.problem: RFC 2190 was the first RTP payload format for ITU-T H.263 video, but the newer RFC 2429 can carry the same streams and more.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recommends moving RFC 2190 to historic status and having new implementations use RFC 4629 and the H263-1998 and H263-2000 media types.
tldr.outcome: The recommendation takes effect on or soon after publication of RFC 4629. Its security picture is unchanged, since both formats refer to the same RTP security texts.

today: RFC 4628 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It recommends that RFC 2190 become historic and that new implementations use RFC 4629.

sections.title: Two Payload Formats for H.263
sections.content:
H.263 is the ITU-T recommendation for video-conference codecs. Version 1, approved in 1996, got an RTP payload format in RFC 2190. In 1998 the ITU approved a new version, known as H.263 plus, with optional features, and its payload format is in RFC 2429.

RFC 2429 can carry streams using only the basic version 1 options. It stated that it does not replace RFC 2190, which continued to be used by existing implementations and might be needed for backward compatibility. Implementations using the new features were to use RFC 2429.
sections.plainLanguage: There were two ways to pack the same kind of video. The newer way can do everything the old way can, plus more.

sections.title: The Recommendation
sections.content:
All H.263 features from the 1996 version are also part of the 1998 and later versions. So RFC 2429 and RFC 4629 can carry new H.263 payloads even when only 1996 features are used.

The memo therefore recommends that RFC 2190 be moved to historic status, and that, as RFC 4629 states, new implementations use RFC 4629 and the H263-1998 and H263-2000 media types. The text says RFC 2429 was being revised to make clear that all new implementations MUST use RFC 4629 for any version of H.263. The recommendation takes effect at, or as soon as possible after, publication of RFC 4629.
sections.plainLanguage: Because the new rulebook covers everything the old one did, the old one can retire and new products should follow the new one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Security considerations for the H.263 video RTP payload are in RFC 4629. Using RFC 4629 instead of RFC 2190 does not change them, because both refer to RFC 3550 and RFC 3551 for security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: Switching to the new rulebook is no riskier, because both lean on the same safety rules.
